description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Lasker Trap. Play 7.e3! and never let ...Bxf3 come with tempo.

drills.briefExplanation: 7.e3! Bxf3 8.Qxf3! dxe3 9.fxe3 — unpin first, then the queen CAN recapture.
drills.description: White to play. Black pins with 5...Bg4 and 6...Qe7 — don't play 7.h3??; unpin with 7.e3!.
drills.explanation: The refutation of the Lasker Trap: 7.e3! unpins the f3 knight BEFORE kicking the bishop. Now 7...Bxf3 is met by 8.Qxf3! — the queen recapture works because the e-pawn vacated e2. After 8...dxe3 9.fxe3 White is simply a pawn up with a solid position; Black's Albin 'compensation' never materializes. The whole trap depended on the e2 pawn blocking the queen — remove the blocker, remove the trap.
drills.name: The e3 Unpin

drills.briefExplanation: 8.Nxf3! Nxe5 9.e3! dxe3 10.fxe3 — the trap is sprung; limit the damage and keep the structure.
drills.description: White to play. The trap is on the board after 7...Bxf3 — find the toughest defense.
drills.explanation: Damage limitation once 7.h3?? is played: 8.Nxf3! is the tougher recapture (8.gxf3?? Nxe5 is crushing, and 8.Qxf3 is illegal — the e2 pawn blocks the queen). After 8...Nxe5 White plays 9.e3!, and after 9...dxe3 10.fxe3 the position is holdable — Black has won the e5 pawn, but White's structure is intact and the bishops will develop. Prevention (7.e3!) beats cure, but this cure beats collapse.
drills.name: Limiting the Damage
